name: Intro: shelf open, logo from the centre
when: The video's first seconds: an animated opening before the first shot plays plain, the closest to the reference video's opening. The trailer shelf of carousel-A2 slides in under the game's logo, which lands big in the centre of the frame and then glides into the top-left corner as the shelf settles, the shelf browses to the long video, the scrubber runs to the moment the video starts on, and that card flies to full frame, its footage already playing: the video's first shot.
anchor: Starts at 0 with the video. The picked card lifts at `lift`; the footage fills the frame 0.7 s later: put that on the first strong word of the voice.
placement: Mount it at the very start (--start 0). `video` is the video's first shot (a clip from the long video, starting at `pick`); the plan's first plain shot follows on from it.

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.game: the game, as logos.json names it (Grand Theft Auto VI)
vars.logo: its logo file, shown in the top-left corner: filled from assets/logos/ by build_video.mjs when `game` is listed there
vars.logo_w: the logo's width in the corner, px (300)
vars.logo_big: the logo's width in the centre, px (760): it lands there on the second frame, while the shelf slides in under it
vars.logo_cx: the logo's visual centre, in logo widths from its image centre (logos.json cx; GTA VI: 0.091): the artwork, not its box, is centred in the frame. build_video.mjs fills it from logos.json
vars.logoat: seconds after the start: the logo glides from the centre into the corner (0.47 s move; 0.6, once the shelf is in; 0.5 to `lift` - 0.6); it leaves toward the left edge with the scrubber
vars.label1: the first trailer's name over its two cards, as written on screen (16 characters at most); label2 the second trailer, label3 the long video
vars.len1: the first trailer's length, m:ss; len2 the same
vars.len3: the long video's length, m:ss or h:mm:ss: the scrubber spans it
vars.pick: where the playhead stops, in seconds into the long video (945 = 15:45); the card of that quarter is the one that flies
vars.card1: trailer 1, first card: a 16:9 still (640x360 is enough), e.g. ffmpeg -ss T -i trailer.mp4 -frames:v 1 -vf scale=640:360:flags=lanczos -q:v 2 card1.jpg. card2 the second; card3 and card4 trailer 2; card5 to card8 the long video's four quarters, in order
vars.back1: optional: the soft back rows, 8 stills of the trailers blurred with ffmpeg (no tint): -vf "scale=640:360:flags=lanczos,gblur=sigma=14" -q:v 3. back2 to back8 the same; empty leaves that soft card out
vars.still: optional: the frame at the playhead stop, full size (1920x1080): the picked card shows it while it lifts, until the footage starts. Empty: the quarter's card still
vars.video: the footage the picked card turns into, a video file starting on the frame at `pick`: it plays from 0.3 s after `lift` to the end
vars.browse: seconds after the start: the shelf browses from the trailers to the long video (1.2 s); at most `lift` - 2.45
vars.lift: seconds after the start: the picked card lifts; the scrubber draws 1.25 s before and the playhead runs during the last 1.0 s. 0.3 s after `lift` the scrubber and names leave (0.13 s) and the card flies to full frame (0.4 s)
vars.out: seconds after the start: the scene ends on the full-frame footage (a cut; the footage fills the frame from `lift` + 0.7)

changed: Only the logo differs from intro-A. In: it lands big in the centre on the second frame (760 px, its visual centre on (960, 500), scale 1.08 to 1 in 13 frames, expo.out, opaque after 6), the move gametag-B was validated with, while the shelf slides in under it; at `logoat` (0.6) it glides into intro-A's corner spot at 300 px (14 frames, power3.inOut), landed at 1.07 s, before the browse. It is drawn at 760 px and scaled down, its shadow scaled so the corner shows intro-A's drop-shadow. Out: 40 px toward the left edge and gone in 7 frames (power2.in) at `lift` + 0.3, as the scrubber leaves (intro-A: a 0.13 s fade). New values logo_big and logo_cx; logoat now means the glide to the corner.
